inputs_basis: CODING-REPEAT-01 nine explicit runs per batch/summary.json (paths from characterization-v3 manifest); same clock domain verified (t_monotonic_ns in samples.json, mini_tool_events.jsonl, mini_status.jsonl)

feasibility_findings.clock: tool events, request events and resource samples all use host t_monotonic_ns; direct alignment without offset guessing
feasibility_findings.resource_semantics: cpu_usage_usec is a cumulative cgroup cpuacct counter (differences give core-s); mem_current_bytes instantaneous, mem_peak_bytes kernel cumulative peak; agent/verifier separate cgroup scopes; 9/9 runs: neg_diff=0, counter_reset=0 (v3), sample gaps recorded
feasibility_findings.event_coverage: 348/348 tool calls identity-paired (v3 strict gates); shared-container background activity cannot be excluded
feasibility_findings.resolution_limit: 263/348 (75.6%) calls are shorter than 0.5s. Existing shared-scope sampling does not support reliable exclusive per-call attribution. Upper-middle tool_duration_s.median values for even counts are excluded.

candidates.question: Container CPU decomposed by event-interval type (pure-request / pure-tool / uncovered / mixed), pure-interval method, no proration
candidates.answered_by_existing: No - characterization-v3 reported time decomposition (durations) and total CPU and top-interval co-occurrence, but not CPU by interval type
candidates.fields_needed: samples.json point series + boundary counters; tool/request intervals - all available
candidates.decision: DONE (the single minimal analysis of this round)

result.only_req_cpu: Zero measured container CPU increment in all nine runs, 82-154 fully request-covered sample intervals each. Does not establish host Agent/API CPU inactivity or a blocking mechanism.
result.only_tool_cpu: 29.1%-91.2% of total run CPU (per-run; medians by task: astropy-13236 11.77, astropy-13398 15.64, django-16485 32.96 core-s)
result.mixed_cpu: remainder 6.26-18.72 core-s (event-boundary intervals, not further decomposable without proration)
result.uncovered_cpu: 0.13-0.21 core-s per run (mostly the final boundary segment)
result.cross_check: per-run totals bit-identical to characterization-v3 cpu_core_seconds (9/9)

candidates.allowed_claims: Container CPU increments grouped by event coverage; only_tool is shared-scope CPU, not exclusive tool consumption. Zero increment applies to only_req sampling intervals and counter precision.
candidates.confounds_not_excluded: Background activity may occur in any category. Host orchestration/API CPU is outside target scope; client-observed intervals, sampling precision and three-task coverage limit interpretation.

candidates.question: Are resource high values concentrated in a few intervals (concentration statistics)
candidates.answered_by_existing: Partially - v3 already reports top intervals by core-rate with overlapping activity categories
candidates.decision: NOT DONE - concentration numbers are threshold-sensitive and add little beyond v3 top-interval reporting; risk of trying multiple cuts

candidates.question: Do high-value intervals across runs of the same task come with different activity combinations
candidates.answered_by_existing: No, but field granularity is insufficient
candidates.decision: NOT DONE - v3 activity_correlations shows most high-value intervals overlap exactly 1 call; category-level combination comparison would rest on n=1 overlaps per interval

candidates.question: Per-tool-call resource attribution
candidates.answered_by_existing: No (and v3 explicitly limits against it)
candidates.decision: Reliable exclusive per-call attribution is not supported by these shared-scope samples; not a universal impossibility claim.

increment_verdict: INCREMENT_FOUND_AND_COMPLETED: one minimal analysis (pure-interval CPU decomposition) with a clear new observation; call-level attribution and high-value combination analyses are closed as infeasible/low-value on this data

single_next_step.recommendation: representative SWE-bench subset behavior analysis (offline, data already downloaded locally)
single_next_step.reasoning: Coding behavior-resource linkage on CODING-REPEAT-01 has reached its data boundary: interval-type level now answered, call-level requires new measurement capability (direction B), more cgroup samples add no attribution/IO/hotspot. SWE-bench subset (selected for task/harness diversity, not success rate) extends Coding behavioral coverage (RQ1/tool-form) with zero new authorization; public Computer/Office measurement preparation depends on user decisions on execution authorization and assets and is not unilaterally started here
single_next_step.stop_condition: subset analysis completes and is registered; no automatic full-corpus expansion, no new adapters beyond the subset need

independent_review.result: Nine-run integer interval decomposition and boundary-counter conservation verified.
